loader_default_vs_named_exports.g1_question: Does the loader read only the default export, or does it also invoke named exports?
loader_default_vs_named_exports.answer_2_1_4: Reads only `.default`. Named exports are never read or invoked. A default export must match a union of { id, effect } or { id, setup }. Shape { id, server } is NOT in the union.
loader_default_vs_named_exports.answer_1_x: NOT PINNED from source. The 1.x runtime loader is not present on this machine (no 1.x CLI binary, no 1.x package containing a loader; the 1.17.3 package contains only type declarations). The only 1.x rule quotable is the type below, which names one default-shaped `server` module and no named-export rule.
loader_default_vs_named_exports.mitigation_status: D2 (export only `default`) is consistent with the 2.1.4 loader, which reads only `.default`. Named exports are therefore inert on 2.1.4; the 1.x named-export rule remains unpinned.

skills_listing_g2.answer_2_1_4: The skill list is prompt TEXT, not a tool description. It is rendered as an `<available_skills>` block, one `<skill>` element per skill with `<id>`, `<name>`, `<description>` children. The `skill` tool description is static and lists no skills. When skills change mid-session, a message reading "The available skills have changed. This list supersedes the previous available skills list." is emitted with the same block.

sources.verbatim_static_tool_description: Load a specialized skill's instructions and resources into the current conversation when the task at hand matches its description.

skills_listing_g2.t7_implication: Read the listing from the assembled system prompt text (experimental.chat.system.transform output.system) by locating the `<available_skills>` block and parsing `<id>` values. Fallback per §2.2 G2: `readSystemPromptListing`. A malformed or absent block yields a named not-measurable reason, not zero.

g6_catalog_lookup.answer: YES. The setup context exposes ctx.model (ModelDomain extends ModelApi: list, default). OpenCode's own built-in plugins call (yield*e.model.list()).data.find((o)=>o.providerID===n.model.providerID&&o.id===n.model.id) inside the context callback. Each catalog entry is Model.Info with limit.context (Int), limit.output, and optional limit.input.
g6_catalog_lookup.list_result_shape: { data: Model.Info[] } (binary reads .data); the reader also tolerates a bare array
g6_catalog_lookup.schema_verbatim: readonly limit: Schema.Struct<{ readonly context: Schema.Int; readonly input: ...; readonly output: Schema.Int; }>
g6_catalog_lookup.consequence: D6: the plugin sends opencode.model.context_limit (reported) when ctx.model.list finds the model with a positive finite limit.context; otherwise it omits it (never 0).
